- **Budget:** Vacant's `before_agent_start` runs after Harbor's. Its `event.systemPrompt` getter renders the prompt including Harbor's forced text (runner.js:1025-1043), so "hard budget of N model turns" can be parsed there. `ctx.getSystemPrompt()` also exists (types.d.ts:249), but I did not check whether it still shows Harbor's text at turn_end.

## (f) Risks

- **Harbor's handler runs first.** At the capped turn it has already aborted; a draft added then is committed (agent-session.js:359) but never sent. So recording a nudge as "sent" at hook time can overstate what the model saw.
- **Clobbering other extensions.** Returning `{continue:false}` or `entries:[x]` overwrites earlier extensions' results (runner.js:678-681).
- **Nudge on the final turn.** At a turn with no tool calls, a draft makes pi continue (canContinue, agent-session.js:463-481). That pre-empts `agent_before_settle` and the Stop rounds.
- **Rounds.**
  - Bumping the shared rounds file (HP:824-843) would use up the Stop check's 2 rounds. Keep a separate counter.
  - A nudge echoed back as a user message without a `VACANT_HEADERS` prefix counts as a new request and resets rounds, which can loop (H:237-239; HP:846-854). In practice this matters for OpenCode's `session.prompt` path (AG:517-519).
- **No lock on `zero_state.json`.** It is read-modify-written without a lock (ZS:55-66, 209-212), unlike `Recorder._lock` (REC:218-225). pi sub-agents are separate processes in the same project and share it.
- **State reset.** `_decide` rebuilds the session entry on a new request (ZS:167), so turn_end counters kept there reset with it. That is the intended per-request behaviour, but keys must not be written back from stale copies.
- **Unsourced pushback after a nudge.** A value that the nudge gets written, if it was derived only in the assistant's text, is not a source: the corpus is prompts, tool outputs and observed files (EV:374-397). The Stop check could then push back `unsourced` and spend turns.
- **Other adapters.**
  - Claude and Codex: new kinds render as no-op (H:136-152), and they register no such event (AG:108-114, 623-624), so they are unaffected.
  - OpenCode: has no hook that lets a turn continue, and `opencode run` exits at the first idle (AG:403-410, 450-451). A mid-run message there would only be a user message in the interactive TUI.
- **Background fresh attempt.** A fresh attempt spawned from the stop hook must finish within the 600 s JS timeout and the 330 s child limit (AG:189; ZS:42). Otherwise the JS kills only its direct child (AG:200), and a detached pi can keep writing `/app/answer.txt` after Harbor has moved on.

Still unknown:
- Whether `ctx.getSystemPrompt()` at turn_end shows Harbor's budget text.
- Whether a draft committed at turn_end reaches the next request when the turn has tool calls. The same mechanism was tested at settle, not at turn_end.
- Whether `session_shutdown` fires after Harbor's abort in `-p` mode.

Pi 0.87.1 confirms all three timing problems. Under Harbor's turn cap, a message Vacant injects on the capped turn is never sent in that run, and `agent_before_settle` is skipped even when the model finished on its own at that turn. The only hook that can still act in `-p` mode is `agent_settled`. It gets exactly one more model call, which goes past Harbor's `max_turns`, so it breaks budget parity between the A and C arms.

**How this was checked.** I ran pi 0.87.1 with the exact `--print --mode json --session-dir --provider --model --extension` shape Harbor uses, against a scripted fake model with no network. The Harbor extension text was copied verbatim with the cap set to 3. A probe extension was auto-discovered from `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/extensions`, which is where Vacant installs. `run_all.sh` reruns everything and writes `results.txt`; line numbers below as `R:n` refer to that file. I did not run the real `vacant.ts`, and I did not run inside Harbor's container.

Path abbreviations used below:
- `PI` = `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vacant/95e2b6b6-418f-504c-a59e-fd594ef13041/scratchpad/agents/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`
- `AS` = `PI/dist/core/agent-session.js`
- `RUN` = `PI/dist/core/extensions/runner.js`
- `TY` = `PI/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`
- `LOOP` = `PI/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js`
- `HP` = `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vacant/95e2b6b6-418f-504c-a59e-fd594ef13041/scratchpad/study/src/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py`
- `AG` = `/home/user/Vacant/vacant_network/adapters/agents.py`

## 1. What `turn_end` returning `{entries:[custom_message], continue:true}` does

- **When it runs.** The loop calls `finishTurn` (`LOOP:179`) before it emits `turn_end` (`LOOP:180`). pi's `finishTurn` then calls `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` (`AS:369-370`), which calls `emitBoundary` (`RUN:662`).
- **How several extensions combine.** Handlers run in extension order.
  - A returned `entries` *replaces* the accumulated array (`RUN:679`). `continue` goes to whichever handler set it last (`RUN:681`).
  - Nothing in that loop checks for abort.
  - So Vacant should return `[...event.entries, draft]`. Today `AG:345` returns `[draft]`, which would overwrite an earlier extension's drafts.
- **Where the message goes.** The drafts are saved to the session unconditionally (`AS:359`). The next request is rebuilt from the saved session (`AS:314`).
  - A `custom` message becomes role **`user`** (`PI/dist/core/messages.js:89-95`).
  - Confirmed: `R:20` shows the request ending `tool → user[VACANT-INJECT-AT-TURN2]`.
- **Whether it adds a turn:**
  - If the turn had tool calls, no extra turn. The message goes out with the next request, and `continue` is ignored because the loop is already continuing (`LOOP:185-188`).
  - If the turn was a final text answer, `continue:true` adds exactly one extra model request (`LOOP:200-203`; confirmed at `R:117`).
  - `continue:true` with nothing to send is rejected (`AS:360-361`).
- **Load order.** Command-line `--extension` paths load first, then everything discovered (`PI/dist/core/resource-loader.js:318`). Among discovered ones, the project's `.pi/extensions` comes before the agent directory (`PI/dist/core/package-manager.js:1989,2007`).
  - Harbor passes its cap via `--extension` (`HP:412-421,450`). Vacant lives in `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/extensions/vacant.ts` (`AG:394`; `/home/user/Vacant/ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py:73`).
  - So **Harbor's handler runs first**. On the capped turn, Vacant's handler already sees `ctx.signal.aborted === true` (`R:10`).
- **Abort beats continue:**
  - In `-p` mode, `ctx.abort()` falls through to `AgentSession.abort` (`AS:2450-2455`). That marks the run as aborted and aborts the agent synchronously (`AS:1610,1617`).
  - With `continue:true`, pi tries another turn, but the OpenAI SDK refuses to send on an already-aborted signal (`PI/node_modules/openai/client.js:357-358`). Only 3 requests reached the fake model (`R:18-20`).
  - The synthetic turn that results has `outcome:"error"`, message "This operation was aborted" (`R:13`), **not** `"aborted"`. Detect the cap with `ctx.signal.aborted`, not `event.outcome`.
  - The same wasted turn also happens with no injection whenever the capped turn had tool calls (exp1b).
- **Can the injected message still arrive?** Not in that run. It stays saved in the session, though, so any later run of the same session sends it (`R:66`).

## 2. After an abort

- **`agent_before_settle` is skipped.** The settle step only runs inside `while (!this._agentRunAbortRequested)` (`AS:1083-1092`), and the post-run step returns false once aborted (`AS:1111-1114`).
  - This holds **even when the capped turn is the model's natural final text answer**: exp3 (`R:68-84`) has no settle event; the uncapped control has one (`R:95`).
  - So the paid batch's C arm missed its check even on runs that finished exactly at turn 15.
- **Events an extension still receives:**
  - The synthetic error `turn_end`.
  - `agent_end` (`AS:715`).
  - `agent_settled`, which is just `{type:"agent_settled"}` with no outcome (`AS:536`, `TY:624-626`).
  - `session_shutdown` with reason `"quit"` (`PI/dist/core/agent-session-runtime.js:296-300`).
- **What works: `pi.sendUserMessage` inside `agent_settled`.**
  - The call is queued while settle handlers are running (`AS:1208-1209`) and executed right after them (`AS:542-546`).
  - It sits inside the original `session.prompt` that print mode is waiting on (`PI/dist/modes/print-mode.js:105`), so it runs before pi exits.
  - exp2 (`R:53-67`): a new run started, one request went out, its bash call wrote `answer.txt=42`, exit code 0.
  - **But Harbor's turn counter is never reset**, so the new run is aborted at its first `turn_end` (`R:56`, `signalAborted:true`). That gives exactly one extra request plus its tool calls, which is **beyond `max_turns`**: 16 calls for C against 15 for A. Unless that is declared, it invalidates the A/C comparison.
- **What does not work:**
  - Plain `sendUserMessage` in `agent_end` throws "Agent is already processing" (`AS:1245`; `R:194`).
  - With `deliverAs:"followUp"` it is queued but never run and is lost at exit (`R:155-174`).
  - `pi.sendMessage({triggerTurn:true})` in `agent_settled` is queued the same way (`AS:1503-1504`) but skips `before_agent_start`. Not tested.
- **Interactive use.** Re-prompting after an abort would override a person pressing Esc. `ctx.mode` distinguishes `"tui"` from `"print"`/`"json"` (`TY:209`). In print mode SIGTERM disposes and exits (`PI/dist/modes/print-mode.js:32-41`), so an abort seen there came from in-process code. Which extension called abort is not knowable.

## 3. What `turn_end` exposes

- **Fields** (`TY:649-656`, plus the shared state at `TY:602-614`):
  - `turnIndex`: counts per run, not per session. It resets at `agent_start` (`AS:712`, +1 at `AS:730`) and restarted at 0 in exp2's follow-up run.
  - `message`: an assistant message whose content blocks are `text`, `thinking` or `toolCall`, plus `stopReason` (`PI/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts:247-269,353-355`).
  - `toolResults`, `messageEntryId`, `toolResultEntryIds`, `outcome`, `entries`, `continue`.
  - `context`: `contextEntries`, `contextMessages`, `llmMessages`, `pendingMessages`, `canContinue`.
- **Harbor's "hard budget of N model turns" line** (`HP:316`) is visible in two places:
  - `before_agent_start` `event.systemPrompt`, which already includes earlier handlers' overrides (`RUN:1032,1043`). Seen at `R:2`.
  - `ctx.getSystemPrompt()` at every `turn_end` (`AS:2474,880`).
  - It was **not** found in `event.context.llmMessages`' system message (`budgetInLlmSys:null`).
- **Caveat.** Matching on Harbor's exact sentence is wiring for the evaluation, which CLAUDE.md product principle 3 rules out.
- **Unknown:** whether gemma's `thinking` blocks appear with thinking off. The fake model sent none.

## 4. Can a settle handler run for ~10 minutes?

- pi has no timeout around extension handlers: they are plain awaits (`RUN:677,722`), and there is no `setTimeout` anywhere in `agent-session.js`, `runner.js` or `loader.js`.
- exp5: a 75-second `agent_before_settle` handler finished and pi exited 0 (`R:118-129`).
- The limits that do exist:
  - Vacant's own stop timeout of 600,000 ms, after which it allows (`AG:189,363`).
  - `CHECK_TIMEOUT_S = 330` (`/home/user/Vacant/vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:42`).
  - Harbor's DABstep agent timeout of 1800 s (`/root/.cache/harbor/tasks/YakWxDW9L9AUkiT2YXQw8d/dabstep-1716/task.toml:17`).

## 5. A child `pi -p` spawned from the extension

- **It works** (exp6, `R:130-152`):
  - Launched with `process.execPath` plus `process.argv[1]`, the same pattern as pi's own subagent example (`PI/examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:249-262`). This avoids needing nvm's PATH (`HP:444`).
  - Passed `--provider`/`--model` from `ctx.model` (`harbor-endpoint`) and inherited the environment. That includes `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and the API key, since `models.json` refers to `"$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"` (`HP:245`).
  - Not tested inside the real Harbor container.
- **The child has no turn cap.** It auto-loads `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/extensions/*`, so Vacant loads in it too. Harbor's `max-turns.ts` sits at `/tmp/harbor-pi-agent/max-turns.ts` and is only passed by flag (`HP:47,50`). The child showed no budget line (`R:152`). This breaks budget parity again.
- **Harbor won't count it correctly.** The child's session goes to `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/sessions/<cwd-slug>/` (`R:153-154`). Harbor reads only the newest `*.jsonl` in its own session directory (`HP:501-510`):
  - If the child writes elsewhere, its tokens are missing from Harbor's metrics.
  - If it writes to the same directory, the child's file would be picked up as the trajectory.
  - The local runner's accounting proxy URL catches every request either way (`/home/user/Vacant/ops/eval/local/run_local.sh:15`).
- **How Vacant's copy in the child knows it is nested:**
  - The parent sets `VACANT_PI_PARENT` in its environment (`AG:301,315,328`) and the child inherits it.
  - The child accepts it only if that pid is one of its ancestors and its cwd is inside the parent's (`AG:282-292`). exp6 confirms the mark pid equals the child's parent pid.
  - A child in the **same cwd** counts itself as a sub-agent: its settle check returns immediately (`AG:342`) and it reports `subagent_stop` (`AG:356`). So a retry there gets no Vacant check.
  - A child in a copied workspace outside that directory becomes a new root session with its own checks.
  - A marker meaning "retry, not sub-agent" does not exist yet.

design:timing-first.summary: v3 的核心是「在預算用完之前提醒先交」。只有同時符合以下條件時，Vacant 才在下一通請求後面加一段三行的提醒，請它先把目前步驟支持的答案寫進檔、之後還可以改：agent 被告知了回合上限（例如 Harbor 在系統提示裡寫「15 model turns」）、只剩 2 回合或 1 回合、這一回合有執行工具、任務要求的檔還不存在。這段提醒搭在本來就要送出的下一通請求上，不多用一通模型呼叫，所以不會超過人設的上限；其他情況下，模型收到的請求和沒裝時逐位元組相同。用付費批次的紀錄模擬：剩 2 回合時，已經說出正確答案卻還沒寫檔的 gemma 有 28 跑（C 組 17 跑），同時最多 3 跑可能被提醒打亂；qwen 一跑都救不到。模型會不會照做沒有重播過。唯一的線索是本機 gemma-12b 試跑：現版交件前檢查因為「檔不存在」退回的 2 跑，下一回合都寫了檔，也都答對，但這只是個案。另外還有三個小改動：剩 1 回合時，交件前檢查只要求寫檔；被上限中止的那一跑也寫一份交件說明給人（現在完全沒有）；修掉一個會把其他擴充訊息蓋掉的錯。不做的有四件：中止後再多問一次、重開一跑、由 Vacant 自己替 agent 寫答案、從模型的文字或思考猜答案。前兩個會超出人設的上限，後兩個不是 Vacant 該做、也做不到的事。要老實說：本機試跑裡「自己說做完卻沒寫檔」比「被上限切斷」多，而前者現版已經在管，所以 v3 在本機可能只多救幾跑，要量了才知道。

design:timing-first.principle_check:
- **Zero-config.** Nothing new to write, set or key. There is no contract, no env var and no budget setting; the budget is read from the same text the model is told. When no budget is stated, M1 and M2 do nothing.
- **Install-minimal.** Arm C3 uses the same two commands a user runs: `pipx install <wheel>` and `vacant install` (ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py:61-73). The updated vacant.ts comes from that same install.
  - BUDGET_RE is a generic pattern (6 positive and 6 negative fixtures), not Harbor's exact sentence.
  - It is disclosed that the only budget source seen in practice is Harbor's sentence: on 33 local first requests it matched only 'budget of 15 model turns' in the system prompt and never the DABstep prompt.
- **Byte-identical when there is no problem.** M1 adds text only when all of these hold: a stated budget, 2 or 1 turns left, a tool turn, not aborted, root session, mode=evidence, and a requested file missing on disk.
  - M2 only changes Stop push-backs that already happen, and only when a budget is stated.
  - M3 never reaches the model.
  - M4 matters only when another extension adds drafts.
  - L-fake scenarios (c), (d) and (g) assert identical request-body sha256.
- **Accountability wording.** The reminder states facts from the record only: the file is missing, and this many turns of the stated budget are left.
  - It says nothing about correctness and names no actor.
  - It passes assert_ks1_clean and feedback_ks1_clean (design/v3a/check_text.out).
  - The delivery note tells the person which file was written after a reminder and that its value was not checked. That covers 'what was checked / changed / not verified'.
  - Measured claims stay at exhibition level, '看得到'.
do_not_do: Do not re-prompt after an abort (pi.sendUserMessage in agent_settled). It makes one extra model call past max_turns (16 vs 15, research exp2 R:53-67) and would override a person's Esc.

Do not relaunch a fresh pi or child pi in v3. The child gets no Harbor cap (R:152) and writes a session Harbor mis-counts (HP:501-510). A child in the same cwd counts itself as a sub-agent and skips checks (AG:342). If relaunching is ever tried, it must be a separately declared arm with its extra cost counted.
Do not let Vacant write the deliverable itself, for example by extracting a value from the final text into answer.txt. Vacant then becomes the author, and nothing checks the value.

Do not detect 'answer in hand' from visible text or thinking. Gemma showed visible text on 0 of 1669 eligible turns in the paid batch, and on 1 of 19 scored local runs. The tool-output detector has 0.52 precision and 6/32 run recall. Thinking is not portable across agents.
Do not send reminders without a stated budget, or at fixed early turns. At K=8 of 15 the simulation gains +11 and puts ≤29 at risk; at K≤8 more is lost than rescued.
Do not inject on the capped turn (ctx.signal.aborted). The draft is saved but never sent, and it would surface as a stale message on resume.
Do not use pi's turnIndex as the budget counter. It resets at every agent_start (AS:712).

Do not record reminders as `review` events, and do not bump the Stop rounds file. Either would skew stop_reached/first-Stop analysis (harbor_vacant.py:48-53, analyze.py:59-64) and use up the Stop's 2 rounds.
Do not return `entries: [draft]` or `continue: false` from any boundary handler. Either overwrites other extensions (runner.js:678-681).
Do not match Harbor's exact sentence, add a VACANT_BUDGET env var, or add any eval-only install step.
Do not spend the remaining paid-API money on DABstep. Use the local machines only.
Do not claim 'Vacant makes the agent better' or 'proves'. Report counts and paired counterfactual runs as 看得到, per 鐵律 5.
design:timing-first.eval_plan:
**Phase 0 (free, before any local run).**
- Unit tests plus the L-fake scenarios (a)–(g) for M1, and M2/M3/M4, with real pi 0.87.1 and a scripted mock model.
- Replay the 316 recorded paid-batch sessions through `budget.nudge` at each turn. Fire counts must match the simulation, for example gemma C: 37 at K=13 and 33 at K=14.
- Gate: all request bodies byte-identical in the no-problem scenarios.

**Phase 1a pilot (w401c-15 only).**
- Setup: gemma-4-12b-it-qat with thinking forced off by orproxy; Harbor pi 0.87.1 with max_turns=15 and model_api=openai-completions, exactly ops/eval/local/run_local.sh.
- 20 tasks × {A, C3} × 1. Look only at mechanism behaviour, not rewards: reminders fire where predicted; every request containing a Vacant header maps 1:1 to a chain budget_nudge or review event (grep the proxy io.jsonl); no infra hangs.
- The pilot2 run now in progress (A vs C1) supplies the A/A′ noise floor and v2's baseline behaviour.

**Phase 1b compliance probe (1003, which is too slow for Harbor runs per RUNLOG §3).**
- Replay the paid-batch gemma contexts truncated at turn 13 with the reminder appended: the 28 reachable runs plus the 16 correct-later 'at-risk' runs. Use reasoning_effort=none and a long client timeout.
- Count next turns that write the file, write the stated value, or write something else.
- This measures whether a gemma-4 model follows the wording. It is not a rescue rate (the context came from a 26b model).

**Phase 2 formal.**
- Pre-register in decisions/ before launch and freeze wheel sha256s.
- Design: 77 tasks (excluding 5 and 70) × arms {A, C1 = current v2 wheel a722a234…392c, C3 = v3} × 3 samples = 693 runs.
- Machines: w401c-15 only; same task and sample on the same machine via run_batch.py; parallel 6. At about 80–290 s per run (pilot progress), that is about 6–7 h.
- Primary: correct deliveries per task averaged over 3 samples. The primary contrast is C3 vs A, which is the product question; the secondary is C3 vs C1, which isolates v3.
- Tests: paired Wilcoxon exact and a sign test via analyze_local.py, with per-sample McNemar. The A-sample-to-sample flip rate is reported as the noise floor.
- Mechanism outcomes, reported alongside the primary:
  - no-answer rate by arm, split into cap-out and natural-stop-without-file;
  - reminders fired;
  - file written after a reminder (compliance);
  - correct after a reminder;
  - rescued = file missing at the reminder and correct at the end;
  - possible harm = a reminder fired and a wrong file was written on a task whose A runs were correct in ≥2 of 3 samples;
  - Stop push-backs and their outcomes;
  - halted-note coverage.
- infra_void: HTTP hangs or 5xx; rerun those cells, excluded from scoring.

**Optional stress run.** max_turns=10, the official DABstep 10-step baseline, A vs C3 × 1.

**Reporting.** Exhibition wording (看得到, not 證明), with per-task counterfactual rows. State plainly if the gain comes mostly from v2's Stop, since natural-stop-without-file outnumbered cap-outs 3:1 among 10 local A pilot runs.

design:redo-first.name: 零設定 v3（pi）：先交、沒交就重來一次（deliver-or-redo ladder）
design:redo-first.summary:
這一版只在一個真的訊號出現時動作：人要求寫出的那個檔，到最後還是不存在。它不讀模型寫了什麼，只看 pi 的生命週期和那個檔。
一跑被回合上限切斷時（沒有人在畫面前的 headless 模式），Vacant 多送一句話：「先把你現在的結果寫進那個檔」。這一步只多一通請求。
寫了還是沒有，就用同一個 pi、同一組啟動參數、同一段原始要求重新開一跑。這一跑不加任何 Vacant 的字，而且不會再重開第二次。
兩步都只在「沒交」時發生，所以不會把已經交出去的答案改壞；沒問題的跑，模型收到的每一通請求和沒裝時逐位元組相同。
付費批次的零花費估算（gemma-26b、思考開）：單用「重開一跑」是 +5～+10 題／77，請求數 ×1.39～1.40。先送那一句的上限是 +11～+21 題，只多 2.6% 請求，但模型會不會照做還沒量過；兩步合起來上限約 61～66／77，請求 ×1.13～1.25。
qwen 兩步都幾乎沒用：它 77 題只有 1 題沒交。qwen 的錯要靠「獨立再算一次、三份投票」才看得到，但成本 ×2 以上、估計淨增 0～2 個百分點，所以這一條先不做。等本機 A 組跑三次、離線算出來值得（至少 +5 個百分點）才做。
評測在人類的 w401c-15 上跑（gemma-4-12b 不思考）：先用正在跑的 pilot2 離線估計，再做 L-fake、模擬使用者、重播與冒煙；過了才跑預註冊的正式批次（79 題×5 次×A/C3，+10 個百分點的檢定力約 0.97）。
要誠實講的代價：重開一跑會超過評測設定的回合預算，所以 C3 和 A 不是同預算比較，成本倍數必須和分數一起報。

mechanisms.what: R0 salvage after a cutoff (same session, one message). When a headless pi run ends because in-process code aborted it (a turn cap) before pi's settle boundary, and the file the request asked for does not exist, Vacant queues exactly one user message asking for the current result to be written to that path. The salvage run is capped by Vacant at 2 model turns. It happens at most once per person request. It uses only pi 0.87.1 APIs the research verified: `agent_settled` still fires after an abort (agent-session.js:531-551), and `pi.sendUserMessage` inside it is deferred and runs before print mode exits (agent-session.js:1208-1210; piexp/results.txt:39-67, where the follow-up wrote answer.txt=42 and pi exited 0). pi skips `agent_before_settle` after an abort (agent-session.js:1083-1092), so this is the only place a missing-output check can still run on the runs that failed in the paid batch.
mechanisms.trigger: On `agent_settled`, only if ALL of these hold: (1) ctx.mode is 'print' or 'json' (types.d.ts:209); (2) root session, meaning no parent_session_id (AG:278-280); (3) `agent_before_settle` did NOT run in this prompt. The flag is set at the top of that handler, before the sub-agent early return. It not running means an abort, because pi runs it whenever the run was not aborted (agent-session.js:1083-1092); (4) no contract and install mode 'evidence' (H:307-317; mode.py:28-42); (5) the person's request names an output path (same regexes as EV.requested_outputs, EV:297-332) and the path as written is missing or whitespace-only. An absolute path is checked with os.path directly (e.g. /app/answer.txt); a relative one against ws; (6) not already salvaged for this request. NOT triggered in any of these cases: TUI or RPC (an abort there is a person's Esc); sub-agents; `vacant do` runs (a contract exists, and vacant do owns attempts); no output named; the file exists; the salvage run itself; a SIGTERM/SIGHUP exit (print-mode.js:31-41 exits without settling).
mechanisms.text_to_agent:
Before delivery: the requested output does not exist yet.
- The request asks for {path as written, e.g. /app/answer.txt}, but it does not exist. Write the result you have now to {path} as your next step, in the format the request asks for. If you are still checking, write your current best result first; you can check further and update the file afterwards.
(KS-1 checked: memory.assert_ks1_clean and feedback.feedback_ks1_clean both pass on this exact text; I ran it with the repo .venv. The quoted path goes through review.q. No actor id.)
mechanisms.cost: +1 model request, plus that request's tool calls, per triggered run; +1 more only if the model does not write on the first. In headless mode, one extra Python spawn per settle: 131-140 ms measured for a no-op hook call. Paid batch requests: gemma A ×1.026, gemma C ×1.028, qwen ×1.002 (design/redo_sim/redo_sim_output.txt:5-6,11-12).
mechanisms.risk: (a) It goes past a harness turn cap by 1-2 requests, so C3 is not budget-matched to A (declared; research §2). (b) The source of the abort is unknowable: it could be the user's own budget extension. That is why the salvage run is limited to 2 turns. (c) A run still weighing two readings may write the other one. This cannot lower the score, because it only fires when the file is missing. (d) The model may spend its one request on another check; the text says 'as your next step'. (e) Whether gemma-12b obeys has not been measured.
mechanisms.l_fake_test:
Use the research harness design/piexp: real pi 0.87.1, mock.py scripted model, Harbor max-turns.ts verbatim with cap=3, and the real generated vacant.ts auto-discovered from $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/extensions.
(1) correct: the mock writes answer.txt at turn 2. Assert that the request bodies (sha256) are identical to a no-Vacant run and that there is no 'redo' event.
(2) capped, never writes; the mock answers the salvage with `echo 42 > answer.txt`. Assert exactly 4 requests, request #4 ending tool→user[SALVAGE_HEADER…], answer.txt=42, one 'redo' event with action=salvage, delivered=true.
(3) the same in TUI/RPC mode, with parent_session_id set, with a contract present, and with the file present. Assert no extra request.
(4) another extension returns turn_end/before_settle drafts. Assert they survive.
(5) pytest: KS-1 on the constant, and the echoed prompt is classified vacant_feedback.
mechanisms.expected_effect:
Paid batch (gemma-26b, thinking on at the proxy), upper bounds assuming it is obeyed:
- Runs that stated a correct value but never wrote it: committed-only A 11 / C 14, committed+leaning A 15 / C 21 (per 77). So +11..+21 per arm (design/redo_sim/redo_sim_output.txt:15-18, built from nudge_sim/manual_audit.json).
- That is more than the report's 8-9 in C (report:345), because the audit also counts 'The result is X' wording (nudge_sim summary).
- qwen +0 (redo_sim_output.txt:8-9).
- The real gain is somewhere in [0, upper bound] and depends on obedience, which is unmeasured. Replay on w401 measures it for free.
- The trigger reads no model text, so it is unaffected by the finding that gemma had visible text on 0/1669 eligible turns (nudge_sim Table 3).

mechanisms.text_to_agent: None added. The child's only user message is the person's original request, byte-for-byte: it is the positional argument already in the parent's argv, which Harbor passes inline (harbor pi.py:450-460). If the recorded request text is not an argv element, as with stdin or @file, Vacant appends the recorded prompt text instead. No Vacant header, no feedback, no mention of the first attempt.
mechanisms.cost: One extra full attempt, only on runs still missing after R0; at most max(T1,6) turns and min(W1,1200) s. In the paid batch, R2 alone gives requests ×1.39 (A-first, 25 extra runs, mean 14.7 requests each) and ×1.40 (C-first) (redo_sim_output.txt:2-3). In dollars that is +58%, because failing runs have long contexts (report:337). After R0 fully obeyed, R0+R2 together are ×1.13-1.25 (redo_sim_output.txt:15-18). qwen ×1.03 (redo_sim_output.txt:8-9). Wall time is about 2× on triggered runs only.
mechanisms.risk: (a) Same cwd, so the first attempt's leftover files are visible. The context is fresh, but the files are not clean (the workspace is 'not a sandbox', RUN:21-24). Absolute output paths such as /app/answer.txt make a copied workspace non-isolating anyway. (b) The harness wall clock (DABstep 1800 s, task.toml:17) may cut the child. No score loss, since nothing was delivered. (c) Repeated external effects: the deny-list is a heuristic. (d) Harbor's metrics miss the child's tokens, because its session is not in Harbor's session dir (harbor pi.py:501-510). Cost must come from the proxy logs (run_local.sh:15). (e) The child launch pattern is proven outside Harbor (piexp exp6) but untested inside the container. (f) It goes past a harness turn budget by design, so it must be declared.
mechanisms.l_fake_test:
Same design/piexp harness.
(1) capped, and the mock ignores the salvage. Assert: exactly one child process; the child's first request user message is sha256-identical to the parent's first user message; the child's session file is under $VACANT_HOME/.../redo/1/ and not in Harbor's --session-dir; the child writes answer.txt=42; parent pi exits 0 only after the child; one 'redo' event with delivered=true.
(2) The child also fails. Assert no second child (VACANT_REDO blocks recursion), a note saying 'not written after one fresh attempt', and total requests = 3+1+child's.
(3) The mock returns HTTP 500 until pi gives up. Assert no child (infra).
(4) The first attempt ran `git push`. Assert no child.
(5) The child hangs past the wall limit. Assert the process group is killed and `ps` shows no orphan pi after the parent exits.
(6) TUI, sub-agent, vacant do, or file exists. Assert no child.
(7) The child without Harbor's --extension. Assert Vacant's own cap aborts it at max(T1,6).
Then a simuser run (ops/eval/simuser, clean container, README install only, pi -p, no contract) with scenarios correct / missing / missing-after-salvage.
mechanisms.expected_effect:
Paid batch (gemma-26b), treating the A and C runs of a task as two independent attempts (method of report §十):
- R2 alone: 50→55 (A-first; matches report:337) and 44→54 (C-first) per 77, i.e. +6.5 to +13 pp (redo_sim_output.txt:2-3).
- R2 after a fully obeyed R0: +0 to +3 more (redo_sim_output.txt:15-18). R2 is the backstop whose value rises as R0 obedience falls.
- qwen: +0 (1 missing run).
- Ladder totals: 61-66/77 against single 44-50, as upper bounds.
- For gemma-4-12b non-thinking, all of this is unknown until pilot2's A s1/s2 give its missing rate.

mechanisms.what: R3 independent recomputation with a majority. GATED: not in the v3 default; built only if an offline gate passes. For requests whose requested output is a short value file (one line, ≤200 bytes), after the first attempt delivered it, Vacant runs one more attempt with the original request in a copy of the workspace that excludes the requested output. If the two values match (numeric relative tolerance 1e-6, else trimmed string), it keeps the first. If they differ, it runs a third. It replaces the delivered value only when the second and third agree with each other and differ from the first. If all three differ, it keeps the first. An absolute output path is snapshotted before each child, the child's value is read, and the original bytes are restored atomically.
mechanisms.trigger: Only if the offline gate passes. The gate: on gemma-4-12b, majority-of-3 over independent plain-pi samples (A s1..s3) beats A s1 by ≥ +5 pp, with a task-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound above 0. If it passes, it also requires headless mode, a root session, not a redo child, no vacant do, the file existing and short, and no external-effect step. Never in TUI, and never for code or multi-file deliverables, where 'agreement' has no meaning.
mechanisms.text_to_agent: None added. Each child gets the person's original request byte-for-byte, the same as R2.
mechanisms.where_in_code: vacant_network/trace/redo.py `confirm()`, sharing the R2 launcher. The workspace copy follows run.prepare_workspace (RUN:143-165) with the COPY_SKIP set plus the requested outputs. The snapshot and restore use atomic_write_bytes. A 'redo' event with action 'confirm' records {values, agree, replaced}.
mechanisms.cost: About 2 + P(disagree) attempts on every short-answer run. The paid batch had qwen string disagreements in 17 of the 76 tasks both runs answered (redo_sim_output.txt:10), so about ×2.2; gemma-26b 3/41, so about ×2.1. Wall time 2-3×.
mechanisms.risk: (a) A harness kill during a child leaves the child's value in the file, because the restore was missed. That is still an answer from the same agent. (b) If the child reads the absolute output path, the runs are no longer independent. (c) Selection can flip a correct first answer: in the paid qwen data the first answer was right in 6 (A-first) or 2 (C-first) of the 8 one-right disagreements (report:340). (d) It does nothing for the 'nothing delivered' failure, which dominates gemma.
mechanisms.l_fake_test: The mock gives values 7/7 → keep, 3 runs. The mock gives 7/9/9 → replace with 9. The mock gives 7/8/9 → keep 7. Kill during child 2 → the file holds a valid value and the event is marked incomplete. Check that the snapshot is restored byte-identically when the value is kept.
mechanisms.expected_effect: Paid batch upper bound if the third run always sides with the correct one: qwen +2 (A-first) to +6 (C-first) per 77, from the one-right disagreements (report:340); gemma-26b about +1/77 (redo_sim_output.txt:4). With a realistic third run, my rough estimate of the net is 0 to +2 pp at ×2.1-2.2. That is dominated by R0/R2 for gemma, which is why it is gated behind measurement on gemma-12b.

do_not_do: Do not parse Harbor's 'You have a hard budget of N model turns' sentence (harbor pi.py:316) or any other harness text. That is evaluation wiring, which product principle 3 rules out. The ladder triggers on pi lifecycle and the filesystem only.
Do not re-prompt or redo in TUI or RPC mode. An abort there is a person's Esc, and a surprise second run takes the person's time and money.
Do not redo when the requested file exists. With no real signal, voting (R3) stays off until the offline gate passes.
Do not add any Vacant text to the redo child's prompt. The past gains came from re-drawing from the original request, and same-session revision bought the least (report:257-260, 300).
Do not let the child outlive pi: run it inside `agent_settled` with a process-group kill (RUN:175-209). A detached child can keep writing /app/answer.txt after Harbor has moved on.
Do not write the child's session into Harbor's --session-dir, where it would be read as the trajectory (harbor pi.py:501-510), or into the workspace.
Do not take C3's cost from Harbor's metrics, which miss the child. Use the proxy logs (run_local.sh:15).
Do not record salvage or redo as 'review' events. That would skew stop_reached (harbor_vacant.py:48-53) and the first-review logic (formal/analyze.py:59-64).
Do not bump the shared rounds file (hookpolicy.py:824-843), and do not return `entries:[draft]` (it clobbers other extensions; runner.js:678-679).
Do not let a redo child count as a sub-agent (strip VACANT_PI_PARENT/SELF), and do not let it redo again (VACANT_REDO).
Do not redo after provider or infra errors, or after external-effect commands (git push, publish, POST).
Do not use machine 1003 for the formal batch (RUNLOG.md:22-27), and do not spend the remaining $1.40 on paid DABstep reruns.

Do not use pilot/pilot2 runs as formal evidence: they shaped the design. Do not claim 'Vacant makes agents better'. The only claim is: 'in headless runs that ended without the requested file, Vacant asked once and/or ran one fresh attempt: +X at ×Y requests'.
design:redo-first.eval_plan:
Compute: only w401c-15 (gemma-4-12b-it-qat), through the accounting proxy in local mode (`/t/<tag>/up/w401/think/off`, run_local.sh:15). The proxy forces thinking off; w401 never thinks (RUNLOG.md:10-11). Before starting, confirm that no response carries reasoning content. Run 4-6 in parallel. Arms differ only by wheel (run_local.sh:6).

Stage 0: no new runs, from pilot2, which is already running (RUNLOG.md:30-33).
- Read only whether answer.txt existed until the design is frozen, then score.
- From A s1/s2, measure gemma-12b's missing rate m and P(the other sample is correct | first missing). This gives the offline R2 estimate and its request multiplier with design/redo_sim/redo_sim.py.
- Go/no-go: if m < 5% of runs, R0/R2 cannot move the score by about 5 pp. Then ship v3 only on the product tests, claim nothing about score, and skip the formal C3 batch.
- Add A s3 (79 runs) to compute the R3 gate: majority-of-3 minus single ≥ +5 pp with a bootstrap lower bound above 0.

Stage 1: product grade, before any batch.
- The L-fake scenarios above (piexp harness, real pi 0.87.1, real vacant.ts) and `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` must pass.
- simuser: clean container → README install → pi -p as usual → scenarios correct (sha256 of request bodies identical to no install), missing, missing after salvage, and TUI (nothing happens).

Stage 2: free realism checks.
- (a) Salvage replay: for every pilot2 A run that hit the cap with no answer.txt, resend its saved session plus the exact R0 text to w401, 3 draws each. Measure P(file written) and P(correct). If P(written) < 0.3, revise the R0 wording before the formal batch.
- (b) Harbor smoke with C3 on 3 tasks that hit the cap in pilot2 (chosen by answer.txt missing, not by reward). Check: the child's requests appear under the same proxy tag; the child session is under VACANT_HOME; no orphan processes; Harbor finishes within 1800 s.

Stage 3: formal. Pre-register in decisions/PREREG_*.md before the first run.
- Setup: 79 pinned tasks × 5 fresh samples (new seed) × {A, C3}, same machine, interleaved with run_batch.py. Harbor pi with max_turns=15, openai-completions, pi 0.87.1, as in the paid batch. Optionally A30 (plain pi, max_turns=30) as a diagnostic arm answering 'is it just more turns?'.
- Primary metric: official-scorer correctness per run.
- Primary analysis: per-task mean over the 5 samples, C3−A, with exact Wilcoxon signed-rank (research.wilcoxon_signed_rank_exact) and a task-bootstrap 95% CI. Secondary: pooled McNemar (flagged as non-independent).
- Power (design/redo_sim/power.py, Beta task model matched to the paid gemma mean 0.62 and a 16/77 two-run flip rate; S=1 reproduces the report's 0.40 at +10 pp, report:227): S=5 gives 0.97 at +10 pp and 0.54 at +5 pp; S=3 gives 0.72 and 0.26 (power_output.txt:2-3).
- Co-primary cost: requests and completion tokens per task from the proxy, including the child, with the multiplier and its CI.
- Mechanism counts: R0 fired / wrote / correct; R2 fired / delivered / correct; infra skips; deny-list skips.
- Invariants, each must be 0:
  - redo fired while the file existed;
  - a Vacant header appears in any request of a C3 run with no trigger;
  - a second-level redo.
- Validity check: C3's realized R2 outcomes compared with the offline 'use another A sample when missing' estimate from the formal A samples. They should agree within noise; a gap means the mechanism is not behaving like an independent attempt.
- Rough time: 790 runs at about 170 s each (pilot2's first run took 166.5 s) over 6 lanes, plus children, is about 7-9 h. This is an estimate; measure it in Stage 2.
- Report quality and cost together, and state that C3 is not budget-matched.

design:signal-first.name: Vacant zero-config v3 for pi: speak only when there is a checkable fact, and while the agent can still act on it
design:signal-first.summary:
v3 的原則很簡單：Vacant 只在有「查得到的事實」時才開口。這些事實是：要求的檔在不在、上限還剩幾回合、測試重跑一次過不過。不再憑推測退回。
最主要的新東西是「截止前提醒」：只有在 agent 被告知有回合上限、只剩最後 2 回合、要求的答案檔又還不存在時，才在那一回合結束插一句「先把目前的答案寫進去，之後可以再改」。沒有上限的跑、或早就寫好檔的跑，模型收到的東西和沒裝時一模一樣。
用付費批次逐回合重建的資料模擬，gemma 每組（77 題）最多救回 12–18 題，最多可能傷到 1–2 題。qwen 完全不受影響，不救也不傷。
第二是被回合上限切斷時，替人寫交件說明（哪個要求的檔沒寫出來），不送任何東西給模型。第三是把「說測過、之後又改了程式」從猜測改成真的重跑一次：只有「原本過、現在不過」才退回，減少誤報。
我也實際量了幾個看起來像訊號、但資料顯示沒用或有害的做法：交出的值有沒有被印出來、同一結果重複出現、空檔案、截止後多給一回合、重開一跑投票。這些都列在不做清單裡。
本機 gemma-12b 的試跑顯示，它常在最後一句話裡說出答案卻沒寫檔。沒裝的 12 跑裡有 3 跑這樣失分；裝了現版的跑，2 次都被既有的交件前檢查救回來。v3 保留這一點，並補上「來不及走到交件前檢查」的那一段。
正式評測建議在 w401 上跑 79 題 × 3 次 × 三組（沒裝／現版／v3），約 13 小時、零花費。主要看 v3 相對沒裝的每題平均正確率。

mechanisms.what: M1 Deliver-before-cutoff reminder. A new pi `turn_end` handler plus a new Python hook kind `turn_check`. It sends at most two reminders per request: after turn N-2 and after turn N-1, where N is a turn budget stated to the agent. It fires only when a requested output file does not exist yet. The reminder is a `custom_message` draft that rides on the next model request, so it adds no extra request. It states facts only (which file is missing, how many turns are left) and never quotes a value.
mechanisms.trigger: All of these must hold. (1) Root session: skip sub-agents, same rule as agents.py:342. (2) The system prompt states a budget N >= 4. It is parsed in `before_agent_start` from `event.systemPrompt`, which already includes Harbor's appended text (research R:3 budgetInEvent='3'). The regex is generic, not Harbor-specific: /\b(?:budget|limit|maximum|max|at most|no more than|up to)\b[^.\n]{0,40}?\b(\d{1,4})\s+(?:model\s+|agent\s+|llm\s+)?(?:turns|steps|iterations)\b/i. design/v3c/budget_regex.py shows it matches Harbor's line (15), matches no pi system-prompt source, and matches 0 of the 79 DABstep instructions. (3) Vacant's own count of `turn_end` events in the process is N-2 or N-1. It increments before any early return, like Harbor's counter (harbor pi.py:319-324); pi's turnIndex is not used because it resets per run (agent-session.js:712). (4) `ctx.signal.aborted` is false. (5) `event.toolResults` is non-empty. A final-text turn is left to the existing Stop check, and firing only on tool turns means no extra turn (agent-loop.js:185-188). (6) On the Python side, install mode is `evidence`. At least one path from `Evidence.requested_outputs` for the current request window (evidence.py:291-333) does not exist on disk, and the path is not a named input (same exclusion as evidence.py:467-471). (7) Fewer than 2 reminders have been sent for this request. The counter is separate from the Stop rounds.
mechanisms.text_to_agent:
Before the turn budget runs out: the recorded steps show a requested output is not written yet.
- The request asks for /app/answer.txt, and it does not exist yet. Model turns left in the stated budget: 2 of 15. Write your current answer to /app/answer.txt now; you can keep checking afterwards and overwrite it if the answer changes.

(The second reminder is identical except it says '1 of 15'. Both texts pass the repo's own `memory.assert_ks1_clean` and `feedback.feedback_ks1_clean`: design/v3c/ks1_check2.py printed OK.)
mechanisms.where_in_code:
agents.py PI_EXTENSION:
- process-level counters TURNS, BUDGET, NUDGES; parse the budget in the existing `before_agent_start` handler (agents.py:314-318);
- a new `pi.on("turn_end")` next to agents.py:341. It calls `ask("turn_check", {...who(ctx), turn, budget})` only when the JS gates pass, so non-firing turns spawn no Python;
- add `turn_check: 20000` to TIMEOUT (agents.py:189);
- return `{entries:[...(event.entries||[]), draft]}`, and apply the same merge fix to the latent clobber at agents.py:345 (runner.js:678-681 replaces entries).

Python side:
- hook.py: EVENT_MAP['pi'] (hook.py:62-64) gets 'turn_check'; a new branch in `handle` next to hook.py:329-331. It is not routed through `_trace` or capture.ACTIONS.
- hookpolicy.py:56 KINDS gets 'turn_check'.
- zerostop.py: a new in-process `turn_check()`, fail-open to allow. State goes in a separate `nudge_state.json` in the project dir, not the Stop rounds file (hookpolicy.py:824-843) and not zero_state.json, which has no lock (zerostop.py:55-66).
- review.py: `render_nudge()` with a KS-1 assert at module load (as review.py:29-30).
- feedback.py:46-47: NUDGE_HEADER added to VACANT_HEADERS.
- recorder.py:49-51 EVENT_TYPES gets 'nudge'. The event is recorded as 'queued': a draft is committed even if a later extension aborts (agent-session.js:359).
- zerostop._write_note (zerostop.py:266-337) gains a line 'Budget reminder after turn K of N: <path> did not exist; it was written at turn J / was still missing'.

Eval readers: ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py:48-53 and ops/eval/formal/analyze.py:59-64 count `nudge` separately from `review`. The L-fake mock learns NUDGE_HEADER (ops/intake/mock_model.py:140-146).
mechanisms.cost:
About 2 days including tests.
- Runtime on non-firing turns: 0 extra processes.
- When firing: at most 2 hook spawns per run. The research measured a hook spawn at 131-140 ms; add the chain read.
- Model cost: 0 extra requests. The draft rides with the next request because the turn had tool calls (piexp results.txt line 20: request ends tool -> user['VACANT-INJECT-AT-TURN2']).
mechanisms.risk:
(a) In runs that never computed the right value, the model may write an unfinished or wrong value instead of nothing. On 26b this is 16 of 71 fires at K=13 ((vi) in nudge_sim run_output.txt line 18). The score is unchanged (0 either way), but the person gets a value. The delivery note marks it as written after a budget reminder.
(b) A run that would have written the right answer at turn 14 or 15 may switch to a worse one. Upper bound 3 of 154 gemma runs at K=13 ((ii)=16 minus 13 already stated).
(c) It only acts when a budget is stated. Plain pi has none, so in ordinary use v3 behaves like v2 here. Say this plainly; it is not a general quality gain.
(d) Request timeouts eat turns. In local C1-62 pilot2, turn 14 was 'Request timed out.', so a reminder can land on an errored request (the committed draft is re-sent with the next request, agent-session.js:314).
(e) Whether gemma-12b obeys is unmeasured. The only local evidence is the Stop reminder: the model wrote on the next turn 2 of 2 times (C1-62 pilot, C1-51 pilot2).
mechanisms.expected_effect:
Paid batch, gemma-26b with thinking on, 15-turn cap. Source: nudge_sim run_output.txt rows K=13/14, manually audited labels. These are upper bounds that assume the model writes the value it already had; obedience is unmeasured.
- gemma A: 34 fires at K=13. Runs that had the correct answer and never wrote it: 11 by K=13, 12 by K=14 (9 committed-only). At risk: at most 2.
- gemma C: 37 fires. Rescuable: 17 by K=13, 18 by K=14 (12 committed-only). At risk: at most 1.
- qwen: 2 fires at K=13, both never-correct. 0 gained, 0 at risk.

Earlier K is worse (gemma A+C): K=8 gains +11 against up to 29 at risk; K=10 gains +19 against up to 15.

Local gemma-12b pilot, 24 non-infra runs (design/v3c/local_m1_sim.py). M1 would fire in 5.
- In 2 the answer was already in hand. C1-51 pilot printed 41679 at turns 9-14, the value that scored 1.0 in C1-51 pilot2. C1-62 pilot2 ended at the capped turn with final text 'Not Applicable', the value that scored 1.0 in C1-62 pilot.
- In 3 the model was still exploring or looping (A-59 pilot, A-2697 pilot2, C1-49 pilot2).

The 12b effect size is unknown until the formal batch.

mechanisms.what: M2 Cut-off delivery note (accountability only; nothing reaches the model). When a pi session shuts down after the budget abort, the Stop check never ran (agent-session.js:1083-1092). Today zero-config writes no delivery.md at all, because hook.py:339-343 handles only the contract case. v3 writes delivery.{md,json} and a chain event. They record that the run ended before the agent said it was done, and list each requested output with whether it exists.
mechanisms.trigger: All of these must hold: `session_end` (pi `session_shutdown`, reason quit); no contract; zero mode is not off; root session; no `review` event after the last step of the current request window. piexp results.txt line 15 shows session_shutdown(quit) does fire after Harbor's abort.
mechanisms.text_to_agent: None; nothing is sent to the model. The note for the person reads: "This run ended before the agent said it was done (the turn budget stopped it), so no delivery check ran. Requested: /app/answer.txt - does not exist." It passes the KS-1 guards (design/v3c/ks1_check2.py).
mechanisms.where_in_code:
- hook.py `handle`: a new zero-config branch beside hook.py:339-343.
- zerostop.py: a new `ended()` that reuses Evidence.window/requested_outputs (evidence.py:210-229, 291-333) with a disk-existence check, and `_write_note` (zerostop.py:266).
- recorder.py:49-51 EVENT_TYPES gets 'delivery_note'.
- harbor_vacant.py `stop_reached` stays review-only.
mechanisms.cost: About half a day. At most one extra cheap hook call at shutdown, inside the existing 30 s session_end timeout (agents.py:189).
mechanisms.risk: Minimal. If the process is SIGKILLed (Harbor's 1800 s agent timeout), shutdown does not fire and there is no note; that is fail-open and the same as today. The wording must not claim the answer is wrong, only what exists.
mechanisms.expected_effect:
Score effect is 0 by construction. Coverage:
- Paid batch: all 28 gemma C cap runs had `stop_reached` false (report line 178), so no note today. All 28 would get one.
- Local 12b pilot: 3 C1 cap runs would get one.

mechanisms.what: M3 Test claim checked by a rerun instead of a suspicion (phase 2, code tasks). Today the `stale` case of `_test_claim` pushes back whenever code changed after the last passing test run (evidence.py:595-605), even if the tests still pass. v3 reruns that same test command twice in throwaway copies rebuilt from the trace (Trace.materialize, blame.py:384): once at the last-pass state and once at the current state, with the hermetic shell (vrun/sandbox.py:165-173), each run at most 100 s. It pushes back only on a flip: the old state passes and the new state fails. It never runs in the live workspace.
mechanisms.trigger: All of these must hold: Stop; zero-config; the `test_claim` sub-case is `stale`; the command matches RUNNERS (evidence.py:61). If both runs fail, or either cannot run or times out, the finding goes to the delivery note only (UNKNOWN).
mechanisms.text_to_agent:
- The final message says "all tests pass", but re-running "pytest -q" on the current files fails: "FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_a" (it passed at step 4, before src/x.py changed). Fix it and re-run, or report that it fails.

(The quote is the agent's own words. The failing line is the tail of the rerun output, at most 80 characters, escaped as in review.q. It passes the KS-1 guards: design/v3c/ks1_check2.py.)
mechanisms.where_in_code:
- evidence.py `_test_claim` (evidence.py:568-606): return the rerun candidate: command, last-pass index, current index.
- zerostop.check (zerostop.py:78-98): run the two reruns inside the existing child process, which has a 330 s limit (zerostop.py:42).
- review.line_for: new `stale` wording (review.py:67-73).
- Honesty boundary to add: a rerun that cannot run is UNKNOWN, never a pushback.
mechanisms.cost: About 1-1.5 days. Runtime only when `stale` fires: at most 2 x 100 s, inside the existing 330 s child limit.
mechanisms.risk:
(a) Trace copies skip .venv/node_modules (SKIP_DIRS, evidence.py:42), so a rerun may fail for environment reasons. The old-state control turns that into UNKNOWN rather than a pushback.
(b) Flaky tests can produce a chance flip.
(c) Long suites time out, giving UNKNOWN, not a pushback.
(d) Tests with side effects are confined to temp copies.
mechanisms.l_fake_test:
A repo with a pytest suite. The mock runs pytest (pass), edits src/x.py, and says 'all tests pass'.
- Variant 1 (edit breaks test_a): one pushback quoting the failing test, then the mock fixes it.
- Variant 2 (edit keeps tests green): no pushback. v2 pushes back here, so this is the removed false positive.
- Variant 3 (a dependency is missing only in the copy): no pushback, and the note says it could not be re-run.
- The live workspace is byte-identical before and after the check.
mechanisms.expected_effect:
DABstep: 0. `test_claim` never fired in the paid batch: the 8 pushbacks were unsourced 6 plus failed_step 2 (report line 219).
Code tasks: the `stale` false-positive class is removed, and real failures come with executable evidence. The size is unknown because there is no data; it needs a code-task eval before any claim.

design:signal-first.principle_check:
Zero-config:
- Nothing to set. The budget is read from what the agent itself was told (its system prompt, through a generic regex). No env vars, contracts or keys.
- Honest limit: M1 does something only when some harness or CI states a turn budget. Plain pi states none, so for ordinary interactive use v3's gain comes from the existing Stop `missing_output` (kept unchanged), M2 and M3.

Install-minimal:
- Same `vacant install`, with no new dependencies (node builtins and Python stdlib only).
- The eval's C arm still does only `pipx install <wheel> && vacant install` (ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py:73). Nothing Harbor-specific is matched: the regex also matches 'at most 10 steps' and 'limit yourself to 20 turns' (budget_regex.py).

Byte-identical when there is no problem:
- On non-firing turns the new `turn_end` handler returns `undefined` without spawning Python. Runs that write the requested output before turn N-2, or that have no stated budget, send exactly what v2 sends. v2 already sends exactly what A sends when there is no finding (report line 160: 157 first-request pairs identical).
- M2 sends nothing to the model.
- M3 only removes pushbacks: it turns the `stale` suspicion into a pushback only on a reproduced flip.
- The L-fake controls check this with sha256 over every request body.

Accountability wording:
- Every new agent-facing line states facts (a file is missing, N turns remain, a rerun failed with this output). None names an actor, uses responsibility or punishment words, quotes a candidate answer, or says the answer is wrong. All pass the repo's own `memory.assert_ks1_clean` and `feedback.feedback_ks1_clean` (design/v3c/ks1_check2.py: 4/4 OK).
- NUDGE_HEADER joins VACANT_HEADERS, so the reminder is never mistaken for a new request from the person or for a source of values (capture.py:206-212).
- The person's delivery note says what was checked, what changed after a reminder, and what stayed unverified, including 'written after a budget reminder'.
do_not_do: Do not re-prompt after the budget abort. That covers `pi.sendUserMessage` in `agent_settled` and any post-cap salvage turn. It spends requests past the operator's cap (piexp exp2, results.txt lines 53-67: one more request, 16 against 15), breaks A/C budget parity, and in the TUI it would override the person pressing Esc. It is rejected on principle even though the ladder upper bound is +11 to +21 of 77 for gemma-26b (redo_sim.py, rerun).

Do not remind early. gemma A+C at K=8: +11 rescuable against up to 29 runs at risk. At K=10: +19 against up to 15. qwen at K=4: 0 gained against up to 89 at risk (nudge_sim run_output.txt). Gemma usually stops right after its first write (85 of 101 runs).

Never quote a candidate value in a reminder or pushback, whether taken from thinking, text or tool outputs. Vacant would be choosing the answer. The tool-output candidate detector was right only 0.52 of the time on 26b (research Table 3). The 12b model shows no mid-run visible text in all but one local run (design/v3a/local_turns.out, vis_text_mid_turns).

Do not add a pushback for 'the delivered value never appears in the agent's own printed outputs'. design/v3c/printed_vs_delivered.py covered 260 written runs of the paid batch. No numeric delivered value was missing from the agent's own tool outputs. All 24 mismatches were categorical or empty answers (yes/no, Not Applicable, letter choices), and 17 of the 24 were correct, so such a pushback would be right at most 0.29 of the time.

Do not add a 'same result came out R times' trigger yet. design/v3c/repeat_sim.py on 26b gemma: R=2 fires 20 times, with 4 rescuable against 9 at risk; R=3 has 1 rescuable against 3 at risk. Re-evaluate offline on 12b A-arm sessions first: 12b does repeat identical commands, e.g. C1-49 pilot2 turns 13-15 and C1-51 pilot turns 9-14.

Do not add an independent second attempt, vote, or fresh redo in v3. Gemma-26b agreed on 40 of 41 tasks where both runs answered (report §十), so there is no leverage there. qwen needs a third run to decide. Locally each attempt costs about 450 s of wall time. After reminder-level rescue, a fresh attempt added only +0 to +3 of 77 at +13 to +25% requests (redo_sim.py ladder). Estimate it for free from the formal batch's 3 A-arm samples before building anything.

Do not push back on an empty answer file. 7 of 79 DABstep instructions say 'If the answer is an empty list, reply with an empty string' (for example dabstep-1753 instruction.md:6). The only empty delivery in the 316 paid runs (qwen C 1753) was deliberate.

Do not store reminder counters in the Stop rounds file (hookpolicy.py:824-843), which would use up the Stop check's 2 rounds. Do not store them in zero_state.json either, which is read and written without a lock. Do not record reminders as `review` events, which would skew harbor_vacant.py:48-53 `stop_reached` and analyze.py:59-64 `evs[0]`.
Do not match Harbor's exact sentence, its /tmp/harbor-pi-agent path, or any eval-only env var, and do not add any install step for the eval (CLAUDE.md product principle 3).
Do not rerun agent tool steps or test commands in the live workspace. rerun.py's honesty boundary is that tool steps are not re-run. Throwaway materialized copies only.
Do not change the existing Stop `missing_output` wording or rounds. It worked 2 of 2 times on the local 12b pilot, and keeping it byte-identical keeps v2 and v3 comparable.
design:signal-first.eval_plan:
Step 0: L-fake, free, before any model run
- The M1/M2/M3 L-fake suites above: real pi 0.87.1, the Harbor max-turns.ts copied verbatim, and the repo mock model.
- Plus the existing tests/test_zero_stop.py, test_zero_evidence.py, test_adapters_agents.py and test_trace_capture.py:217-227. These must still pass: their exact-string checks on the extension are kept.

Step 1: offline replay on real 12b sessions, free
- On the pilot2 A-arm pi sessions still running now (A and C1, 79 tasks x 2), rebuild per-turn answer-file existence as in design/v3c/local_m1_sim.py.
- Count where M1 would fire, and read each fired run to label it rescuable, at risk, or never-correct.
- Also compute the repeat-trigger trade-off on 12b; it is deferred in do_not_do.
- Proceed to step 2 only if rescuable exceeds at-risk.

Step 2: formal local batch
- Pre-register it in decisions/PREREG_* and freeze the wheel sha256 before launch. The human signs.
- Rule 5: before this batch, only say 'visible improvement'.
- Setup:
  - DABstep formal_79 (ops/eval/pilot/tasks.json).
  - Model gemma-4-12b-it-qat with thinking off, forced at the proxy with reasoning_effort=none; confirm at the endpoint, not only from pi's flag.
  - Harbor pi 0.87.1, max_turns=15, model_api=openai-completions (ops/eval/local/run_local.sh).
  - w401c-15 only (RUNLOG §3: 1003 is slow, and two 300 s stalls happened there).
- Arms:
  - A: no Vacant.
  - C1: v2, the efda0d1f wheel used in pilot2.
  - C2: v3.
- Samples: S=3 per task and arm, giving 711 runs.
- Scheduling: run_batch.py gives the same machine per task and sample, a shuffled order, and never reads rewards.
- Duration:
  - pilot2 runs took about 400 s each at parallel 6, about 53 runs an hour, so about 13 hours.
  - Consider parallel 4, because request timeouts already ate turns in 2 of 24 pilot runs. Log timeouts per arm as infra.
- Primary metric:
  - Per-task mean reward over the 3 samples, C2 minus A.
  - Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (research.wilcoxon_signed_rank_exact), alpha 0.05.
  - Power with S=3, from redo_sim/power.py (I reran it; it models the 26b batch's spread): 0.26 at +5 pp, 0.72 at +10 pp, 0.98 at +15 pp.
- Secondary, Holm-corrected: C1 minus A (v2's existing Stop missing_output; the local pilot suggests this may already be large), and C2 minus C1 (what v3 adds).
- Mechanism logs, per arm:
  - Reminders fired.
  - Obeyed: the requested output exists by the end of the run after a reminder.
  - Rescued: the first write came after the reminder, and the answer is correct.
  - At risk: a reminded run ended wrong on a task where A was correct in at least 2 of 3 samples.
- False-positive labelling:
  - Every Stop pushback is labelled TP or FP. FP means the deliverable was already correct at push time; a missing file counts as TP.
  - Pre-registered demotion rule: any pushback kind with at least 2 FPs and an FP share above 1/3 becomes note-only in v3.1.
- Invariants, where a failure voids that arm:
  - At most 15 model requests per run in every arm, checked from the proxy ledger by tag.
  - The first request body is sha256-identical between A and C2 for each task and sample.
- Noise baseline: flip rate between A's own samples (A vs A').
- Free v4 estimates from A's 3 samples, with no extra runs: 'redo if missing' (sample 2 used only when sample 1 wrote nothing) and a 3-sample majority vote. These decide whether a fresh-attempt or vote mechanism is worth building.
- Report tokens and requests per arm from ledger/summary.json. Do not use the paused pilot runs for any claim.

評比（1–5 分，5 最好；各項依據寫在 build_list 的 rationale 裡）：
- 設計一（預算快用完時提醒先交、最後一回合只退回缺檔、被切斷的跑也寫交件說明、修掉蓋掉其他擴充訊息的錯）：救回 4、誤動作 4、產品原則 4、pi 可行性 5、成本 5（請求數 ×1.00）、可用腳本模型測 5。
- 設計二（切斷後多問一次、還沒交就重開一跑、投票）：救回 5、誤動作 5（只在沒交時才動）、產品原則 2（會超過操作者設的回合上限，還要在 Harbor 容器裡開子 pi）、可行性 3、成本 2（重開一跑的請求數 ×1.39–1.40）、可測 3。
- 設計三（同樣的預算提醒、切斷說明、測試重跑）：救回 4、誤動作 4、產品原則 5、可行性 4、成本 5、可測 4。

決定：做一個合併版 v3（評測叫 C2），全部在回合預算之內，不多一通模型呼叫。照順序做：
1. 修掉會把其他擴充訊息蓋掉的錯，只改兩行。
2. 核心是預算提醒，四個條件都成立才發：
   - agent 的系統提示寫了回合上限；
   - 只剩最後 2 或 1 回合；
   - 這一回合有跑工具；
   - 要求的檔還不存在。
   這時在下一通本來就要送出的請求後面加三行：「先把目前最好的答案寫進去，之後還可以改」。其他情況下，模型看到的東西和沒裝時一模一樣。
3. 只剩 1 回合時，交件前檢查只退回「缺檔」這一項，其他的寫進交件說明。
4. 被上限切斷的跑，也寫一份交件說明給人。現在這種跑完全沒有說明。
5. 評測前先過產品等級關卡：
   - 付費批次 316 跑重播的觸發次數要和模擬一致；
   - 模擬使用者在沒問題的情境下，每一通請求要逐位元組相同；
   - 評測腳本把新事件分開算。
6. 寫一支免費的「照不照做」探針。

預期效果：
- 付費批次模擬（gemma-26b，開思考）：C 組最多救回 17–18 跑，只算明確說出答案的是 12 跑；最多傷到 1 跑。qwen 救回 0 跑，也傷不到。
- 本機 gemma-12b（不思考）：試跑紀錄裡它沒有任何可讀的中間文字；被上限切斷的跑多半在重複同一類 grep／awk 指令，手上不一定有答案。它在本機最常見的失敗是自己說做完了卻沒寫檔，這一點現版（C1）已經在管：試跑裡退回 3 次，3 次都寫了對的答案。所以 v3 在本機能多救幾跑還不知道，要量。

不做：
- 切斷後再多問一次：會超過上限，16 通對 15 通。
- 重開一跑：請求數 ×1.4，也沒在容器裡驗過。等正式批次 A 組的三次樣本離線估過，值得才做。
- 投票、測試重跑、從模型文字猜答案、提早提醒、Vacant 自己寫答案。

評測：
- 機器分工：w401 跑正式批次，79 題（分析用 77 題）× 3 次 × A／C1／C2，共 711 跑。照試跑速度估約 19 小時，零花費。1003 處理長提示太慢，不跑 Harbor，改跑照不照做的探針。
- 主要指標：每題 3 次的平均答對率，C2 減 A，用精確 Wilcoxon 雙尾檢定，α＝0.05。
- 次要指標（Holm 校正）：C1 減 A、C2 減 C1。
- 檢定力：真實差 +10 個百分點時約 0.72，+5 個百分點只有 0.26。
- 預註冊要人類簽字；簽字之前只能說「看得到」。

The child launch is untested inside the Harbor container. Harbor's metrics miss the child (HP:501-510). A child in the same cwd counts itself as a sub-agent and skips its checks (agents.py:282-292,342).
After reminder-level rescue it adds only +0..+3 of 77 (redo_sim_output.txt:15-18).
Gate for a v4 with its own preregistration: in the formal batch, C2's residual no-answer rate is ≥10% of runs, AND the offline 'use the next A sample when the first is missing' estimate from A's 3 samples is ≥+5 pp with a task-bootstrap lower bound >0.

rejected.idea: R3 independent recompute and majority vote (D2, gated).
rejected.why:
About ×2.1–2.2 cost (D2).
It can flip correct first answers (report:340). Gemma-26b disagreed on only 3 of 41 double-answered tasks (redo_sim_output.txt:4), so there is almost no leverage there.
Estimate it for free as majority-of-3 over the formal A samples before building anything.

rejected.idea: Test-claim rerun of `stale` in materialized copies (D3 M3).
rejected.why:
There is no observed instance, and it cannot be measured on DABstep: test_claim never fired in the paid batch.
The current `stale` push-back is grounded by definition: the claim has no supporting recorded run after the last code change (evidence.py:595-605).
It would add up to 2×100 s of test execution inside the Stop child.
Revisit as v3.1 with a code-task L-fake. Keep it out of the frozen C2 wheel so C2 vs C1 isolates V3-2..4.

rejected.idea: Reading the budget from the person's prompt (D1 M1 fallback).
rejected.why: Nothing enforces a budget stated there. Plain-prompt phrases like 'up to 5 steps of the manual' are false-trigger risks. Only the system prompt, which a harness or CI sets, is used.

For gemma A+C at K=8: +11 rescuable against ≤29 at risk. At K=10: +19 against ≤15. For qwen at K=4: 0 against ≤89 (design/nudge_sim Table 1).
Gemma ended within one turn of its first write in 85 of 101 writing runs.

rejected.idea: Detecting 'answer in hand' from visible text, thinking, or tool outputs, or quoting a candidate value in the reminder.
rejected.why:
Gemma-26b had visible text on 0 of 1669 eligible turns. The tool-output detector had 0.52 precision and 6/32 run recall (nudge_sim Table 3).
Local 12b text blocks are the empty template marker '<|channel>thought\n<channel|>' on every tool turn (my dump of pilot2 A-49/C1-49/C1-62/A-2697 sessions).
Quoting a value would make Vacant choose the answer.

rejected.idea: Vacant writing the deliverable itself (e.g., extracting the final text into answer.txt).
rejected.why: Vacant would become the author, with nothing checking the value. That contradicts 'accountability of each step' and makes the claim 'Vacant does not judge answers' false.

On 26b, R=2 fires 20 times: 4 rescuable against 9 at risk (design/v3c/repeat_sim.out:1). R=3 gives 1 against 3 (line 2).
12b does loop (pilot2 A-49 and C1-49 turns 8-15), but with no answer in hand.
Re-evaluate offline on the formal A-arm sessions.

rejected.idea: Push-back on an empty answer file, or on 'delivered value never printed'.
rejected.why:
7 of 80 pinned DABstep instructions allow an empty string (grep; e.g. dabstep-1753/instruction.md:6).
Printed-vs-delivered mismatches were categorical or empty answers, most of them correct (design/v3c/printed_vs_delivered.out).

rejected.idea: Matching Harbor's exact sentence or the /tmp/harbor-pi-agent path, adding a VACANT_BUDGET env var, or adding any eval-only install step.
rejected.why: CLAUDE.md product principle 3: the C arm uses only `pipx install <wheel>` + `vacant install` (ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py:61-73).

rejected.idea: Recording reminders as `review` events, bumping the Stop rounds file, or keeping reminder state in zero_state.json.
rejected.why: `review` events would skew stop_reached and first-Stop analysis (harbor_vacant.py:48-53, formal/analyze.py:59-64). Bumping the rounds file would consume the Stop's 2 rounds (hookpolicy.py:824-843). zero_state.json is read-modify-written without a lock (zerostop.py:55-66).

rejected.idea: Running Harbor batch cells on 1003, or spending the remaining paid key on DABstep.
rejected.why:
1003 has 26 s median / 150 s p90 latency on long prompts, and two 300 s header-timeout stalls polluted failure classes (RUNLOG.md:22-27).
The remaining $1.40 cannot fit a round and cannot detect +5 tasks (report §十一).
Local compute is free.

risks: Compliance is unmeasured. Every rescue number is an upper bound that assumes the model writes the value it already had. For 26b, 8 of the 28 reachable runs were only 'leaning' and may write the other reading (nudge_sim manual_audit). V3-6 measures this on 12b before the formal batch.

The paid-batch simulation does not transfer to local 12b. The sim used gemma-4-26b with thinking on at the proxy. On 12b the capped runs look like loops of near-identical grep/awk commands (pilot2 A-49, C1-49, A-2697 turns 8–15), where the answer may not be in hand. V3-2 may then turn 'missing' into 'wrong': score-neutral, but a value the person now sees. The delivery note must say it was written after a reminder and not checked.

The main local lever may already be v2. In pilot2 so far, the A arm's natural-stop-without-file (A-51, A-62) is caught by C1's Stop missing_output, and the 3 local push-backs were each followed by a correct write (design/v3c/local_classify.py rerun). The C2−C1 difference may be near 0 even if C2−A is positive. Do not credit v3 for v2's effect.

The 'byte-identical when there is no problem' claim must be restated. V3-2 changes requests in runs that would have written at turn 14–15 anyway: 16 of 94 successful gemma-26b runs first wrote at t14–15 (run_output.txt:125). The correct wording is 'identical whenever no check point finds a missing requested output'. Update the CLAUDE.md 口徑 line accordingly.

V3-2 is inert in ordinary use. The only budget source seen in practice is Harbor's system-prompt sentence (BUDGET_RE matched 0 of 79 DABstep instructions and no pi system-prompt source, design/v3c/budget_regex.py). Any measured gain applies to budget-stated headless contexts only.

Load-order dependency. Harbor's --extension handler runs before Vacant's (resource-loader.js:318). If some harness instead registered its cap after Vacant, a draft on the capped turn would be saved but never sent. This is mitigated because reminders go only at N-2/N-1, never at N, and are recorded as 'queued' and confirmed from the proxy io.jsonl.

Request timeouts on w401 eat budget turns and can swallow the request that carries a reminder. 'Request timed out.' turns appeared in pilot2 C1-49 (turn 7) and C1-62 (turn 14). The draft is re-sent with the next request, but a turn is lost. They are logged per arm, with a sensitivity analysis and a parallelism cap.

After a reminder, the Stop check may push back `unsourced` on a value that came only from the model's reasoning (evidence.py:374-397). That spends turns. V3-3 limits this when ≤1 turn is left, but at 2 left it can still happen. Label every such push-back TP/FP in the batch.
Unknown: whether pi print mode awaits the session_shutdown handler before exit. If it does not, V3-4 notes go missing. The L-fake detects this, and the fallback is agent_settled.
Throughput. 711 runs is about 19 h on one machine (pilot2 mean 570 s per run at parallel 6). A drop to parallel 4 means about 28 h. 1003 cannot share Harbor cells (RUNLOG.md:22-27).
Power. At S=3, +5 pp is detected only 26% of the time (power_output.txt:2), so a null result is not evidence of no effect. The prereg must state this in advance.
Pilot contamination. The design was shaped by pilot and pilot2 outcomes. The formal batch must use fresh samples with a new prefix and seed, and no pilot run may be cited as evidence (鐵律 5).

The KS-1 and new-request loop. If NUDGE_HEADER were missing from VACANT_HEADERS, an echoed reminder would count as a new person request and reset the rounds (hook.py:235-248; hookpolicy.py:846-854). The V3-2 unit tests must assert the classification.
